Query: When is repeat lumbar fusion indicated for symptomatic pseudoarthrosis?
Policy Name: Cigna Lumbar Fusion (CMM-609: Lumbar Fusion with Decompression)
Referred Sections: CMM-609.8: Repeat Lumbar Fusion (Arthrodesis) at the Same Level)

Required findings: Greater than six (6) months elapsed since the prior lumbar fusion
Daily pain of clinically significant intensity causing functional impairment (e.g., inability to perform household chores, prolonged standing)
Physical examination findings that are concordant with the reported symptoms

Less than clinically meaningful improvement despite BOTH a six‑week trial of prescription‑strength analgesics (including steroids, gabapentinoids, NSAIDs) AND a six‑week provider‑directed exercise program (physical therapy, chiropractic, osteopathic or physician‑prescribed)

Post‑operative imaging performed ≥6 months after the index fusion that demonstrates pseudoarthrosis at the requested level(s) (plain radiographs, CT or MRI) and imaging findings that correlate with the patient’s symptoms
Absence of unmanaged significant mental or behavioral health disorders (e.g., major depressive disorder, chronic pain syndrome, secondary gain, opioid or alcohol use disorder)
Documentation of nicotine‑free status either as a never‑smoker or cessation ≥6 weeks prior to the planned repeat fusion verified by objective cotinine testing (serum, urine or saliva)
Medical necessity indications.Source: CMM-609.8: Repeat Lumbar Fusion (Arthrodesis) at the Same Level > Symptomatic Pseudoarthrosis

Non-Indications: Less than six (6) months since the prior lumbar fusion
Pain or functional limitation that does not meet the threshold of clinically significant daily impairment
Failure to demonstrate pseudoarthrosis on imaging or imaging not concordant with symptoms
No documented trial of both appropriate pharmacologic therapy and structured exercise program for the required six‑week duration
Active tobacco use without documented cessation or without objective cotinine verification
Presence of unmanaged significant mental or behavioral health disorders
Imaging performed earlier than six months post‑op
Patient does not meet nicotine‑free verification requirements
Important criteria & exceptions: Nicotine‑free status may be satisfied by never‑smoker status or by documented cessation ≥6 weeks with a normal cotinine level (serum, urine or saliva)
Both pharmacologic and exercise conservative therapies must be completed for a minimum of six weeks unless contraindicated
Imaging must be obtained at least six months after the index fusion to reliably assess pseudoarthrosis
If pseudoarthrosis is identified intra‑operatively, imaging criteria may be waived per general guidelines for intra‑operative instability
Behavioral health clearance is required only for unmanaged disorders; stable, treated conditions are acceptable
Documentation required: Operative report of the original lumbar fusion (including level(s) fused and instrumentation used)
Post‑operative plain radiographs (flexion‑extension views) performed ≥6 months after the index surgery
CT or MRI report confirming pseudoarthrosis and correlating neural element compression at the same level(s)
Detailed physical examination note documenting findings that match the patient’s pain pattern
Medication administration record showing at least six weeks of prescription‑strength analgesics, steroids, gabapentinoids and/or NSAIDs
Physical therapy/chiropractic/osteopathic progress notes confirming a supervised exercise program of ≥6 weeks
Objective cotinine test result (serum, urine or saliva) within normal range performed ≤6 weeks before the repeat surgery request
Behavioral health evaluation note confirming no unmanaged significant mental or substance use disorder
Smoking cessation documentation (if applicable) confirming ≥6‑week abstinence
